>
> Probably an unrelated bug, but the function stanc in rstan always sets the model name to "anon_model" because
> rstan:::legitimate.model.name <http://legitimate.model.name> is set to always return "anon_model".

>

On 8/17/12 12:35 AM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Thanks. That is just an unimportant function not implemented.

> But if you do think that is a bug, please let me know
> what problem it would cause.

If you don't need different model names for the R interface,
I'd suggest hiding the legitimate.model.name() function from
users, assuming that's even possible in R. For developers,
a little doc that it's meant to be constant might help.

Also, if we don't need different model names, there shouldn't
be any function arguments for other functions related to model
names. (I didn't look to see if there were.)

In general, we don't want any non-functional stubs in the
release versions. They just confuse users.

- Bob

parts:
I'm sorry for bringing this up on this thread.  The context in which I came across this problem was while attempting to compile stan models into shared objects without using the inline package.  The code I used to do that is https://gist.github.com/3376975. 

I was able compile the so just fine. But, because the model name was defined as "anon_model" even though I gave it another name, when I attempted loaded the module with Rcpp the class that I was expecting to have in the shared object was not there, or rather it was there, but named something else.
